title: Sabalenka wins in China and works on being kinder to herself
summary:
Aryna Sabalenka began her China Open tournament with a win over Mexico's Renata Zarazua. She also spoke about trying to be kinder to herself when she plays tennis.

Sabalenka, ranked number two in the world, won 6-1, 6-3. The match lasted 63 minutes. She hit 11 aces. An ace is a serve that lands where it should and that the other player cannot touch.

It was her first match since losing her world number one ranking and her US Open title to Elena Rybakina in September.

Sabalenka's most recent titles came in March. She won Indian Wells and the Miami Open one after the other. Winning both tournaments is called the Sunshine Double.

Sabalenka said expecting more from herself can sometimes push her forward. But it can also use up her energy. She said she was working on being easier on herself.

Her next opponent was set to be Czech player Nikola Bartunkova in the third round. Bartunkova had come close to beating Sabalenka at the Berlin Open in June.

Tennis matches are divided into sets. Sabalenka won both sets against Zarazua to move on in the tournament.
why_it_matters: The story shows how a successful athlete thinks about expectations and the energy they can take.
